Subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling, concurrency & queue sizing — follow-up

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for a productive call earlier — really helpful to hear how your team at Acme is planning to scale the contextual search and live-chat summarization features. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goals: 95th %-ile token latency < 200ms for chat flows, predictable throughput for nightly batch re-ranking jobs, and secure VPC private deployment.
- Current baseline (from call): ~1.2M daily queries (peak 1.8M), average request size ~450 tokens, re-rankers run in batches overnight (8-10M embeddings/day).
- Key constraints: strict data residency, 4-week pilot target, and requirement for no user-facing latency spikes during peak.

Action items we agreed:
1) I will share a short Sizing + Autoscale proposal that covers: baseline GPU pool size, concurrency limits, queueing/backpressure behavior, and expected latency curves.
2) Your infra/contact (Priya) to share a demand profile CSV with hourly traffic for a 7-day sample + any SLOs you want enforced.
3) Loop in our infra architect (Aditya) for any network/KMS questions once we land on the draft.

Attached: sample proposal template (we'll fill with your numbers) — feel free to replace placeholders.

Would Thursday (6/24) at 10am PT work for a quick follow-up to review the draft?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sam / Priya — looping in Aditya and Dev to confirm the sizing assumptions and auth/network plan. Initial read from the demand profile: average hourly QPS at peak day ~75 QPS sustained during 11am-2pm PT, short spikes to ~140 QPS for a few minutes during events, and nightly bulk re-rank embedding jobs that need ~1.2 GPU-days of compute within a 6-hour window.

Aditya / Dev — proposed starting point (we'll refine after you confirm):
- Dedicated GPU pool for low-latency chat: 8x A100-style instances (mixed 80/20 for redundancy), target per-instance concurrency cap of 48 active requests, model pinned to r-infer-16k-8bit (or equivalent) with KV cache enabled.
- Autoscaling policy: scale up in 1-2 instance increments when 75% average utilization across pool over a 5-min window; scale-down after sustained <30% for 15 minutes. Burst queueing: allow short in-memory queue (max 500 concurrent queued requests across pool) with graceful backpressure (429 + Retry-After) if queue depth exceeds threshold.
- Embeddings/re-rankers: separate reserved pool (4x T4-style or quantized instances) with batching window tuned to meet 6-hour SLA overnight; autoscale based on queued batch size.
- Auth/network: support OIDC short-lived tokens + KMS key-wrapping; VPC peering with customer-managed subnets and egress rules.

Can you validate the above and call out obvious gaps? Also confirm any hard limits your infra team must enforce on concurrency or connection count.

If this looks reasonable, Sam — can we confirm 6/24 10am PT to go over the detailed PDF with numbers filled in?

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling, concurrency & queue sizing — follow-up

Thanks for the detail — good signal from the CSV. A few technical confirmations and refinements below: 

1) Concurrency & per-instance sizing
- The suggested cap of 48 active requests per A100-equivalent is reasonable for r-infer-16k-8bit with KV cache, assuming average request ~450 tokens and most requests are streaming. If you expect long-context (>8k) requests frequently, we should reduce concurrency per instance ~25-30 to keep latency tail predictable.

2) Autoscaling policy tweaks
- For production SLOs, we recommend a slightly more conservative scale-up threshold: trigger scale up when 70% average utilization over 3 minutes to proactively add capacity during fast-growing spikes. Keep scale increments at 1 instance to avoid overshoot. Use a 10-minute cool-down for scale-up to prevent flapping during bursty minutes. Scale-down: start after 20 minutes below 25% with gradual step-downs (1 instance at a time).

3) Queueing/backpressure
- Implement two-tier queues: in-memory short queue (max 500 queued requests) and a persistent rate-limited queue for longer tails (SQS-style) with token-based fairness to avoid head-of-line blocking. Configure a per-request max wait time of 2s in in-memory queue before demoting to persistent queue; return 429 when persistent queue depth exceeds safe threshold and include Retry-After header.

4) Embeddings/re-rankers
- Separate homogeneous pool: 4x quantized T4-style nodes should meet the ~10M/day goal if batch sizes are tuned and parallel workers coordinate sharding. Add ephemeral burst capacity policy to double workers during the 2-hour peak ingestion window if necessary.

5) Auth & network
- OIDC short-lived tokens supported. We'll integrate with your KMS via customer-managed key wrapping over our private peered network. Need VPC subnet CIDR ranges + egress rules from Priya to validate firewall rules.

Next steps:
- Marissa: I can convert these notes into the sizing PDF by end of day and include a small table with expected latency curves at 50/95/99 %-iles for different concurrency knobs.
- Priya: please share VPC subnet ranges and any connection limits (max concurrent TCP connections per IP) you must enforce.
- Sam: confirm 6/24 10am PT or propose alternate slot.

Happy to hop on a call with your infra team to walk through the queueing/backpressure design.

—Aditya
